name: Queen's Gambit Declined
blurb: The classical answer to the Queen's Gambit: Black holds d5 with ...e6 and develops solidly. A sound choice that has stood up at the highest level for over a hundred years.

ideas.d4 d5: Claims the centre and stops White from playing e4 for free.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 e6: Supports d5 with a pawn. Very solid, though the c8 bishop is shut in for now.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6: Develops and adds a second defender to d5.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7: Blocks the line from g5 to the queen, so the f6 knight is no longer pinned.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O: Castles before the centre opens, so the king is safe.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 N: The knight supports f6 and gets ready to help with ...c5 or ...e5 later.
Strengthens d5 and blunts the rook's pressure on the c-file.
Black waits until White's bishop is on d3 before taking on c4, so the bishop must move again to win the pawn back.
Offers piece trades. Black's position is a little cramped, so swapping pieces makes it easier to defend.
The freeing break. It challenges White's centre and will open lines for the c8 bishop.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5 exd5: Against the Exchange, recapturing with the e-pawn opens the c8 bishop's diagonal.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 c5: The Semi-Tarrasch. Black hits d4 at once and aims for free piece play rather than a cramped defence.
